subject: technology
topic: Smartphones are fundamentally altering the way we process spatial information
angle: While externalizing navigation to GPS technology is linked to a decrease in hippocampal functional connectivity, it does not appear to affect actual navigational abilities.
title: The cost of digital navigation

hooks.text: Where does your internal map go?
You navigate perfectly but your brain connectivity drops.
You have outsourced your sense of direction to a screen.
A blue line moves across a glass screen.

reveal.headline: GPS use is linked to lower hippocampal connectivity.
reveal.body: Using GPS navigation in AR glasses for three months showed a decrease in functional coupling between the hippocampus and associated brain regions. The evidence on this is emerging.

explain.headline: Brain changes do not equal lost skills.
explain.body: While brain connectivity changes, researchers observed no effect on actual navigational abilities. The study on connectivity was limited to three months and did not observe any impact on cognitive skills.

matters.headline: Your brain maps are changing.
matters.body: That may be why your internal sense of place feels different. Your brain might be prioritizing external data over internal structural connections.

example.headline: The familiar drive home.
example.body: You sit in the passenger seat. You watch the blue line move on the screen. You do not look at the landmarks outside the window. You do not think about the turns. You just follow the line to your front door.

question.headline: Where would you go if the screen went dark?

claims.text: The experimental group showed a decrease in functional coupling between the hippocampus and associated brain regions after three months of using GPS navigation in AR glasses, while the control group showed an increase.
claims.quote: the experimental group showed FC decrease after three months of using GPS navigation implemented in AR glasses in contrast to FC increase in the control group without such intervention.

claims.text: No effect of using GPS navigation in AR glasses was observed on navigational abilities.
claims.quote: Importantly, no effect of intervention on navigational abilities was observed.

claims.text: No significant differences emerged between experts and novices, nor females and males, for the retrieval of spatial information presented on 2D maps with a simple design and content.
claims.quote: no significant differences emerged between neither experts and novices, nor females and males for the retrieval of spatial information presented on 2D maps with a simple design and content.

claims.text: Analysis shows that paths tend to be drawn more frequently at first but soon decrease in frequency in favour of landmarks.

claims.text: Nodes, boundaries, and districts tend to be drawn throughout the drawing process but are much less frequent.

verdict: The evidence shows that technology-assisted navigation is associated with measurable changes in brain connectivity but does not currently show a measurable degradation in spatial navigation skills.
caveat: The study on hippocampal connectivity was limited to a three-month period and did not observe any impact on actual cognitive navigational abilities.
caption:
Technology is changing how your brain connects to the physical world.

Research shows that three months of GPS navigation in AR glasses is linked to a decrease in hippocampal functional connectivity. However, the study did not find any actual degradation in navigational abilities and was limited to a three-month period.

Do you still know the way home without your phone?
